22455: • Every classroom must be equipped with a sensor that continuously measures carbon dioxide in the air, within 6 months.,- Maximum limit set at 1000 ppm of CO2, lowered to 800 ppm during a declared pandemic period.,- The department must publish the sensor data on its website every week.,- An action protocol must be applied by schools when the CO2 standard is exceeded.,- Every classroom must have an air exchanger or purifier, supplied and paid for by the department, within 12 months.,- Exchangers and purifiers must be inspected at least every six months, with reports made public.,- The department must ensure annual follow-up on corrective measures taken as a result of inspections.
22465: • Requires the government to set by regulation a maximum number of patients per nurse, licensed practical nurse and orderly,- Applies to emergency departments, surgery, general and specialized medicine, as well as long-term care centres (CHSLDs),- Creates a 7-member advisory committee to recommend these ratios to the government,- The committee includes representatives from unions, professional orders and institution management,- The committee must submit a report on the impact of the regulation, first in 2023 and then every 5 years,- This report must be tabled in the National Assembly and studied by a committee,- The government has one year after the Act is assented to in order to adopt the regulation on ratios
22471:
• Adds to the preamble of the Charter the importance of preserving a healthy environment for human health.
  • Recognizes the right of every person to live in a healthy environment that respects biodiversity.
  • Elevates this right to the status of a fundamental right, like the other rights in the Charter.
  • Removes the restriction limiting this right to the measures and standards provided for by law.
  • This change could facilitate legal recourse based on this environmental right.
22581:
• Amends the Act respecting educational childcare services to guarantee the right to these services.
  • Removes two paragraphs from section 2 of the Act, which limited the scope of this right.
  • The Act would come into force five years after its assent.
22597:
• Makes special educational projects and concentration programs free of charge in public schools, up to $5,000 per year.
  • Includes in the free-of-charge provision selection fees, file-opening fees, test administration fees, and staff training fees.
  • Prohibits school service centres from establishing a special project school in more than one building.
  • Except in special cases: several buildings are permitted only if they are located no more than 250 metres from one another.
22599:
• Amends the Act respecting the Generations Fund, intended to reduce Québec's public debt.
  • Sets a capitalization threshold of $100 billion for this fund.
  • Requires that the allocation and amounts of the Fund remain unchanged until this threshold is reached.
  • Exceptions remain possible only where the Act itself provides for them.
  • The Act would come into force on the date of its official assent.
22639: • The Minister of Finance will have to ensure gender equality and diversity are considered in budgetary decisions.,- A report on gender- and diversity-based impacts must be tabled after each budget.,- This report must also be tabled after an economic update announcing new measures.,- The competent parliamentary committee must study these tabled reports.,- The Minister of Finance will publish an annual analysis of the gender- and diversity-based impacts of fiscal measures.,- The President of the Treasury Board will also publish a similar annual analysis of government spending.
22711:
• Requires that the two-thirds vote of the National Assembly come from at least two recognized parties.
  • Applies to appointments and removals of the Québec Ombudsman, the Auditor General and the DPCP.
  • Also applies to the appointment of the heads of the Commission d'accès à l'information and the Autorité des marchés publics.
  • Affects positions related to police, anti-corruption efforts and lobbying.
  • Also applies to the Chief Electoral Officer and certain public service positions.
  • Amends 13 different acts to add this multi-party representation requirement.
  • Prevents a single majority party from reaching the required qualified majority on its own.
22765: • Requires the school to provide equivalent educational services if it cannot provide the services required by law.,- Applies to students with handicaps, social maladjustments or learning disabilities.,- Requires the authorization of the parent or guardian for a minor student.,- These services must aim at the full development of the student's personality and social integration.,- Aims to develop fundamental skills that foster the student's autonomy.,- The school service centre must ensure that the student can continue on a path toward a secondary school or vocational diploma.
22767: • Every adult would be presumed to consent to the donation of organs and tissue after death, unless a refusal was expressed.,- The person responsible for the removal would have to verify with relatives that no refusal was expressed during the person's lifetime.,- This verification would not be required in an emergency attested by two physicians to save a life.,- The register managed by the Régie would be renamed to include both consents and refusals.,- The forms would inform people of the presumption of consent and their right to refuse.,- Minors under 14 years of age would remain subject to mandatory consent from a parent or guardian.,- The register kept by the Chambre des notaires would also be renamed to include refusals.
22797: • Requires elementary schools, secondary schools and adult education centres to adopt a policy against sexual violence within one year.,- The policy must include mandatory training, security measures, a complaint process and psychosocial support services.,- Imposes a code of conduct to govern relationships between staff and students, including students of full age.,- Sets maximum time limits: 7 days to intervene, 90 days to process a complaint or report.,- Requires the formation of a committee including management, staff, students and parents to develop and review the policy.,- Provides for annual accountability reporting on complaints, training and sanctions applied.,- Allows the minister to impose oversight or have obligations carried out by a third party at the institution's expense in cases of non-compliance.
22799:
• The Caisse de dépôt should ensure that its investments have sustainable social and environmental impacts.
  • Its mission now explicitly includes the sustainable economic development of Québec.
  • The annual report submitted to the Minister of Finance must detail the social and environmental impacts of investments.
  • This report must be tabled in the National Assembly before April 15 each year.
  • The government may set out by regulation the criteria for assessing these impacts.
  • A regulation may also specify how these impacts must be publicly disclosed.
22831:
• The Minister will be required to take temporary residents into account in multi-year immigration planning.
  • The multi-year policy directions will target the number of persons admitted on a temporary or permanent basis.
  • The annual plan will have to specify the expected number of temporary residents, in addition to permanent immigrants.
  • The number of selection decisions provided for in the annual plan will also cover temporary stays.
22899:
• Renders invalid lease clauses that prohibit pets.
  • Applies to leases already in effect, not only to new leases.
  • The government must remove prohibition mentions from mandatory lease forms within 30 days.
  • The definition of "pet" is based on the Animal Welfare and Safety Act.
  • Other existing tenant protections in the Civil Code remain unchanged.
23167:
• Adds an official emblematic insect for Québec, the white admiral (Limenitis arthemis arthemis).
  • Amends the Act respecting the flag and emblems of Québec to include this new symbol.
  • Comes into force upon assent of the Act.
23285:
• Requires authorization from the Minister of the Environment before adding a project to the Québec infrastructure plan.
  • The Minister must refuse a project that jeopardizes the achievement of Québec's greenhouse gas reduction targets.
  • The government will set out by regulation the criteria for analyzing climate impacts, with the assistance of environmental experts.
  • The Minister may impose conditions or restrictions to reduce emissions related to a project.
  • The Minister may amend or add conditions to a project that has already been authorized, if necessary.
  • The Québec infrastructure plan will have to include a report on the emissions and climate impact of projects.
  • Public bodies will be required to provide the Minister with the information necessary for this climate assessment.
23425:
• Prohibits evicting a tenant for the purpose of converting their dwelling into short-term tourist accommodation.
  • Amends section 1959 of the Civil Code of Québec to add this exception.
  • Aims to protect tenants against the conversion of residential dwellings into tourist rentals.
  • The act would come into force on the date of its assent.
23753: • Requires CEGEPs, universities and other educational institutions to adopt a study-family-work balance policy.,- Policy intended for student parents or caregivers, to be adopted within 6 months and implemented within 12 months.,- Creates special statuses: student parent, caregiver, deemed enrolled or enrolled full-time.,- Provides for leaves, exam accommodations and measures facilitating access to childcare services.,- Requires a joint committee consulting affected persons to develop and review the policy.,- Requires institutions to report annually to the minister on the implementation of their policy.,- Allows the minister to impose oversight measures or have obligations carried out at the institution's expense in cases of non-compliance.
23955:
• Creates a citizen initiative right requiring the BAPE to hold a hearing if a petition reaches certain thresholds.
  • Requires 40,000 signatures (including 5,000 per region, in 3 regions) for a national issue, or 15,000 for a regional issue.
  • The chair and vice-chair of the BAPE will be appointed by the National Assembly, following an in-camera interview with MNAs.
  • Allows the BAPE to require a report on a project's greenhouse gas emissions and its reduction measures.
  • The government will have to publicly justify authorizing a project despite a refusal recommended by the BAPE.
  • Abolishes the Comité consultatif sur les évaluations environnementales stratégiques, whose tasks are transferred to the BAPE.
  • Gives the BAPE the power to recommend that a project be subject to a full environmental assessment.
24137:
• Amends the Act to Foster the Economic and Social Inclusion of Persons and Families to Overcome Poverty for recipients of the Social Solidarity Program.
  • Allows these recipients to earn employment income without a reduction in their benefit.
  • Aligns the amount of permitted employment income with that of the Basic Income Program.
  • The Act would come into force on the date of its official assent.
24211:
• Creates the position of Parliamentary Budget Officer, appointed by the National Assembly for a non-renewable seven-year term.
  • This officer provides non-partisan analysis of Québec's public finances, budget forecasts and economic trends.
  • The officer must produce an annual report on economic outlooks, a portrait of public finances twice a year, and a report on intergenerational equity every three years.
  • Transfers responsibility for certifying the pre-election report on public finances from the Auditor General to this new officer.
  • Members of the National Assembly may request a confidential assessment of the cost of a proposed expenditure or measure.
  • Departments and public bodies must provide the officer with requested documents and information, notwithstanding access to information legislation.
  • The officer and staff benefit from judicial immunities and are bound to secrecy regarding confidential data.
24223: • Prohibits driving with a blood alcohol level of 50 mg to 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.,- Immediate licence suspension upon a first offence within this new blood alcohol range.,- 3-day suspension for a first offence, 7 days for a second offence within 5 years.,- Suspension of at least 90 days for a third or subsequent offence within 5 years.,- Licence recovery conditional on an assessment of the person's relationship with alcohol or drugs.,- Possible requirement to complete an alcohol or drug awareness program.,- Possibility of requiring the installation of an ignition interlock device in certain cases.
24279:
• Grants each Member the right to visit certain administrative institutions (departments, municipalities, schools, hospitals, etc.).
  • Allows the Member to speak confidentially with any person on site, except ministers.
  • Authorizes the Member to be accompanied by an employee, an expert, and a journalist during the visit.
  • Limits visits to once every three months per institution, for a maximum of two consecutive days.
  • Requires written notice of at least 10 business days before the visit.
  • Allows the institution to refuse or restrict the visit only for serious security reasons.
  • Provides for recourse to the Superior Court if a refusal is deemed unjustified.
24453:
• Aims to reduce food waste by half by 2030 through a national strategy.
  • Requires businesses and manufacturers to offer their unsold goods to organizations before discarding them.
  • Creates a public registry of unsold goods quantities and donation agreements reached.
  • Prohibits deliberately rendering unsold food or goods unfit for consumption.
  • Creates a Repair Fund to encourage the repair of goods and the circular economy.
  • Prevents manufacturers from refusing a warranty if the good was repaired by a third party.
  • Provides for fines of up to $250,000 (individuals) or $1.5 million (businesses).
24543:
• Specifies the order of flags: the fleurdelisé on the left, or in the centre if three flags are displayed.
  • Requires a public ceremony for Flag Day in every RCM or isolated local municipality.
  • Allows the minister to appoint inspectors to verify compliance with the Act.
  • Requires the Québec flag on federal buildings, national parks and municipal parks in Québec.
  • Requires the flag on the building housing the riding office of provincial and federal members.
  • Sets out the rules for disposing of a worn flag (dignified burning or cutting into strips).
  • Requires members to provide a Québec flag free of charge to anyone who requests one.
24617:
• Extends the right to install surveillance mechanisms to users of rehabilitation centres, not just CHSLDs.
  • Targets 4 types of centres: intellectual disability, physical disability, dependency, youth in difficulty.
  • For a user under 14 years of age, the camera must be installed by their representative.
  • Consent to surveillance of a user under 14 years of age must come from their representative.
  • The institutions concerned will have to inform new users of this right upon admission.
  • Adjusts posting and information obligations to include the rehabilitation centres concerned.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
24727: • Adds a new section 45.1 to Québec's Charter of human rights and freedoms.,- Enshrines the right of every person to decent housing.,- This right includes security of tenure, availability, accessibility and affordability of housing.,- Draws on international instruments recognizing the right to housing (UN, OAS).,- The Act comes into force on the date of its assent.
25171: • Sets the objective of achieving carbon neutrality in Québec by 2050.,- Requires the government to take the necessary measures to reduce GHG emissions.,- Imposes a reduction target of at least 37.5% compared to 1990, increasing with each period.,- Requires a review of the targets every five years.,- Allows the government to set different targets depending on the sector of activity.,- Provides for public consultation in a parliamentary committee before setting or revising a target.,- Requires a public opinion from the advisory committee on climate change before any parliamentary consultation.
25237:
• Creates a national digital identity managed by the Minister of Cybersecurity and Digital Technology, with digital credentials.
  • Specifies that the use of the digital identity cannot be imposed by a public body to obtain a government service.
  • Establishes a national digital identity register to store and share government data between bodies.
  • Prohibits the Minister from using this data for the purpose of profiling individuals.
  • Requires public bodies to use the Minister's cybersecurity services and to report breaches of their data.
  • Gives the Minister the power to develop a telecommunications network and connectivity infrastructure for the State.
  • Removes the requirement for Treasury Board authorization for building lease contracts related to the Minister's telecommunications.
25291:
• Creates a special parliamentary committee of 5 members to study the documents from the Grenier inquiry on Option Canada.
  • The committee identifies which documents must remain confidential, with unanimous consent required.
  • Documents not deemed confidential are made public in the committee's final report.
  • The committee may retain a special adviser to make recommendations on the confidential nature of documents.
  • The Chief Electoral Officer must transmit the documents within 30 days of assent.
  • Documents deemed confidential will automatically become public after 25 years.
  • No civil action may arise from facts revealed as a result of this Act.
25363:
• Recognizes the right of older persons to remain at home for as long as possible, with appropriate support.
  • Guarantees rights: affordable and adapted housing, protection against abuse, dignified end of life, financial security.
  • Establishes a national strategy for the autonomy and home care of older persons.
  • Requires the government to adopt a five-year action plan with concrete targets for care and housing.
  • Provides for a first action plan to be published within six months of the Act's passage.
  • Assigns the Commission des droits de la personne to ensure respect for these new rights.
  • Provides for tax measures, rent regulation, and financial support for low-income seniors.
25393:
• Makes all women or pregnant persons in Québec eligible for health insurance and prescription drug coverage, regardless of their migratory status.
  • Eliminates the usual waiting period under health insurance for women or pregnant persons.
  • Grants eligibility if the person intends to remain in Québec for more than 6 months, including 2 months after childbirth.
  • Maintains coverage for 2 years after the expected date of childbirth for persons not otherwise eligible.
  • Provides for 12 weeks of eligibility following a pregnancy termination.
  • Requires a medical certificate confirming the pregnancy and expected date of childbirth for registration.
  • Provides that the Act comes into force on the date of its assent, with transitional rules for ongoing cases.
25575: • Allows municipalities to claim compensation from the government for land transferred to a school service centre.,- The compensation corresponds to the value of the land as entered on the property assessment roll.,- Extends from 45 to 60 days the time limit for municipalities to give their opinion on school planning.,- Requires school service centres to prioritize optimal density of land use.,- Gives the minister the power to cancel the obligation to transfer land if densification is not prioritized.,- Reduces existing compensation by the amount of any compensation already received for the same land.
25631:
• Creates a common school network bringing together public schools and "contracted" private schools that choose to join it.
  • Prohibits any selection of students upon entry into schools within this common network.
  • Gradually cuts public funding for private schools that refuse to join the common network.
  • Requires free tuition and equal funding for all schools in the network, including special educational projects.
  • Establishes catchment-area school maps, with one designated school per address, reviewed annually.
  • Provides for compensation measures to reduce socio-economic inequalities between school catchment areas.
  • Requires contracted schools to maintain financial transparency, undergo external audits, and be subject to oversight by the minister.
25709:
• The SAAQ will have to send a notice of payment 30 days before the deadline for vehicle registration.
  • A similar notice will also have to be sent 30 days before the driver's licence renewal deadline.
  • These notices must comply with the form and content determined by the SAAQ.
  • An owner or licence holder cannot be found guilty of driving without a valid right if the SAAQ did not send the required notice.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
25793: • Students, parents, employees and service providers must have their faces uncovered in schools and school services.,- Ban on the wearing of religious symbols expanded to school service centre staff and certain contractors.,- Prayers and religious practices prohibited in premises made available to schools and centres.,- New mandatory rules of conduct against bullying related to racism, sexual orientation, gender or disability.,- Teachers required to submit a teaching plan, to be evaluated annually by the principal.,- Creation of a committee on the quality of educational services in each school service centre.,- Certain provisions apply notwithstanding the Quebec Charter and the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
25795:
• Requires the SAAQ to enter into agreements with departments to enforce certain Acts.
  • Concerns the Taxation Act, immigration, labour standards, occupational health and safety, and transportation.
  • Amends section 519.65 of the Highway Safety Code to remove certain existing paragraphs.
  • The Minister of Transport designates the departments or agencies covered by these agreements.
  • The Act comes into force upon official assent.
25919:
• The landlord must apply to the Tribunal to set the rent if the increase exceeds a regulatory threshold.
  • The notice of increase must detail the new rent and the increase in dollars and as a percentage.
  • The notice must specify that the rent will be set by the tribunal beyond a certain percentage.
  • The exemption period for new or converted dwellings is reduced from five to three years.
  • The Minister of Housing may suspend certain rent-setting criteria for a given year.
  • The Tribunal will annually set mandatory increase percentages based on the dwelling's heating method.
  • A tenant's acceptance of an increase no longer prevents the rent-setting procedure before the tribunal.
26021: • Allows an officer to be designated as a worker if they personally perform work elsewhere, revises the calculation of benefits,- Establishes a possible negotiation process between parties following a request for administrative review at the CNESST,- Increases fines, particularly for breaches of confidentiality related to injuries caused by violence, including sexual violence,- Sets maximum time limits for grievance arbitration and encourages the use of mediation before arbitration,- Requires unions to present their audited financial statements to members every year,- Broadens the grounds for absence for reservists and allows for absence in the event of a disaster or public health decision,- Adds two members to the CNESST's board of directors and provides for separate temporary rules for the education and health sectors
26023:
• The Minister of Housing will have to create a committee every five years on rent criteria.
  • The committee will make recommendations on the criteria and percentages for setting or adjusting rent.
  • Its members will be chosen in equal numbers from among representatives of tenants and landlords.
  • The Minister appoints members from lists provided by interested organizations.
  • A mediator or conciliator will preside over the committee's work.
  • The committee's mandate ends no later than September 1, after which the committee is dissolved.
  • The first committee must be formed 30 days after the assent of the Act.
26065: • Prohibits requiring union membership as a condition of employment in a collective agreement.,- Eliminates the counting of union membership numbers; only a secret ballot vote confirms representativeness.,- Requires an absolute majority of the votes of employees, not just of those voting, for certification.,- Requires a certified association to have its certification reconfirmed by secret ballot vote after each collective agreement or arbitration award.,- Requires the submission of audited financial statements to the Minister of Labour each year, before June 30.,- Requires the Minister to publish these financial statements on his website within 30 days of receiving them.,- Members may obtain a free copy of their association's financial statements upon request.
26067: • Right to telework for up to 40% of hours if the nature of the work allows it.,- The employer may require telework of up to 40% if this is provided for at hiring.,- The 40% threshold may be exceeded with authorization from the Commission or by mutual agreement.,- Employer and employee must agree on a telework plan including flexible scheduling.,- Mandatory reimbursement of expenses: 50% or 100% depending on the case.,- Prohibition on using remote surveillance software, except for supervised visits with advance notice.,- Employer must adopt a telework policy, and a recourse is provided in case of disagreement.
26073: Supervised consumption sites outside Santé Québec facilities must obtain authorization from the minister.,Prohibition on authorizing a site within 150 metres of a school, a CPE, or a daycare.,The minister consults the ministers of Education and Family, and the municipality, before authorizing a site.,The authorization lasts 4 years, is renewable, and may be revoked in case of non-compliance with the conditions.,The minister may impose conditions to ensure cleanliness, sanitation, and safety around a site.,Prohibition on opening a school, a CPE, or a daycare near an already authorized site.,Sites existing on the date of assent are automatically deemed authorized for 4 years.
26079: • Makes access to several contraceptive methods free of charge through a new program administered by the RAMQ.,- Allows any minor to consent alone to the prescription or administration of contraceptives.,- Authorizes pilot projects to delegate to other professionals the right to prescribe contraceptives.,- Requires each region to distribute condoms free of charge in secondary schools, CEGEPs and universities.,- Provides for culturally appropriate measures for access to condoms among First Nations and Inuit.,- Requires the Ministère de l'Éducation to integrate sexuality and relationship education into school curricula.,- Gives midwives the power to prescribe, dispense and administer contraceptives.
26093:
• Optimizes the tax credit for career extension of experienced workers
  • Reduces the maximum age of a child eligible for the childcare expenses tax credit
  • Extends the tax credit for the digital transformation of print media
  • Abolishes the tax credit for synergy between Québec businesses
  • Abolishes certain tax holidays for the recruitment of specialized employees
  • Standardizes the insurance premium tax rate with the sales tax rate
  • Increases the exemptions used to calculate the prescription drug insurance premium
26095: • Divides Québec into territories where each family medicine department must affiliate all residents with a medical setting.,- Makes general practitioners collectively responsible for taking charge of patients affiliated with their clinic.,- Introduces capitation-based remuneration (a fixed amount based on the number and vulnerability of patients taken charge of).,- Creates a composite remuneration method (capitation, hourly rate, fee-for-service) for general practitioners working in private practice or CLSCs.,- Adds a "collective supplement" to remuneration tied to the achievement of access-to-care targets set by regulation.,- Allows financial penalties for physicians who record erroneous diagnoses that affect their remuneration.,- Provides for a patient de-affiliation mechanism in certain cases (relocation, lack of capacity, breach of trust).
26097:
• This private bill concerns a person named Joseph Paul-Émile Daniel Michel Marcil.
  • The text provided is an administrative procedure, without details on the actual content of the act.
  • It is not possible to summarize the concrete changes, as the content of the bill is not included.
26099:
• Adds to the Québec Charter a right to the discoverability of French-language cultural content and to access to it.
  • Requires certain digital platforms (video streaming, music, audiobooks, podcasts) to register with the Minister of Culture.
  • Requires that the interface of platforms, televisions and connected devices be in French by default.
  • Requires certain devices and platforms to provide access to French-language content and platforms according to regulatory criteria.
  • Creates a Bureau de la découvrabilité des contenus culturels within the ministry to oversee the application of the Act.
  • Provides for fines of up to $300,000 and administrative monetary penalties for non-compliance.
  • Allows the Minister to enter into agreements with platforms providing for alternative measures to the legal obligations.
26101: • Allows any municipal council with at least 12 councillors to create an executive committee with delegated powers.,- Requires every municipality to appoint an officer responsible for buildings, the environment and urban planning.,- Requires that documents useful for decision-making be provided to elected officials as soon as notice of a special meeting is given.,- Facilitates densification near rail-based public transit stations, without the possibility of a referendum.,- Allows a municipality to issue a permit before full payment, in exchange for a financial commitment from the applicant.,- Reduces the number of representatives from the Montréal agglomeration on the council and executive committee of the CMM.,- Allows the Ville de Québec to delegate certain heritage powers to the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation.
26111:
• The Minister must prepare an overview of the presence of "forever chemicals" in water, sludge and leachate.
  • Municipalities and operators of water systems or landfill sites must have samples tested in an accredited laboratory.
  • An assessment report must be tabled in the National Assembly and updated at least every five years.
  • The government will then have to adopt regulatory standards following this assessment.
  • These standards will set maximum permitted concentration thresholds for forever chemicals.
  • Periodic follow-up testing will be mandatory, with remediation measures required in cases of exceedance.
  • The government will also determine penalties, and the standards will be reviewed every five years.
26135: • Creates the position of "secretary for the selection of independent administrative decision-makers," appointed for 10 years by the National Assembly.,- Requires a written competition and an interview before a selection committee to become an administrative decision-maker in a tribunal or board.,- Requires 10 years of relevant experience to be eligible as an administrative decision-maker.,- Sets the normal term of a decision-maker's mandate at 5 years, with annual performance evaluation.,- Creates a decision-makers' remuneration committee that reassesses their conditions every 4 years.,- Standardizes ethical rules and subjects all decision-makers to the Conseil de la justice administrative.,- Amends 14 acts affecting various tribunals (housing, labour, transportation, police, energy, etc.) and repeals several existing regulations.
26161:
• Adds a member with expertise in digital creativity to the SODEC board of directors.
  • Creates the Digital Creativity Commission, to be established within six months of assent.
  • Allows SODEC to create subsidiaries to carry out its financial and investment activities.
  • Authorizes SODEC to set its own fees, commissions and professional fees.
  • Expands the financial services offered: loans, guarantees, investments, grants and repayable assistance.
  • Renames the Conseil national de l'audiovisuel as the "Audiovisual Commission."
  • Removes the requirement to have two director generals dedicated to specific cultural fields.
26257:
• Allows the sale and use in Québec of products that comply with the standards of another Canadian province or territory.
  • The government may, by regulation, exclude certain products from this principle and publish the list online.
  • Qualified workers authorized elsewhere in Canada may obtain professional recognition without significant additional requirements.
  • The government may require, by regulation, additional training or an examination for certain trades or professions deemed to be at risk.
  • Professional orders retain the power to impose conditions to protect the public, despite facilitated mobility.
  • The Office des professions du Québec must oversee the professional orders and may require corrective action to ensure labour mobility.
  • The government may adopt or amend a regulation in place of a professional order in order to comply with its interprovincial commitments.
26411: • Cooperatives may be operated in the interest of a community identified in their bylaws.,- The number of members may no longer be lower than the minimum number of founders required for incorporation.,- Preferred shares must be registered, with transfers subject to board of directors' approval.,- A new "reserve for potential patronage rebates" may be created to stabilize the payment of patronage rebates.,- It becomes prohibited to sell a cooperative's assets for less than their market value.,- Mergers are broadened between cooperatives or federations that do not share the same purpose, with fewer financial requirements.,- A member of a housing cooperative who resigns or is expelled loses their right to remain in the rented premises.
26623: • Requires employers of certain categories with 50 or more employees to establish a joint ecological transition committee.,- At least half of the committee members must represent non-management employees.,- The committee issues recommendations on environmental performance, green jobs and climate justice.,- The employer must provide financial, social and environmental information requested by the committee.,- A biennial report on subjects determined by regulation must be produced by the employer.,- The committee meets at least once every three months, with 28 annual hours per member.,- The employer must justify in writing, within three months, the follow-up given to the committee's recommendations.
26625:
• Creates a Constitution of Québec affirming its primacy over incompatible laws and defining the Québec nation.
  • Establishes secularism, the civil law tradition and the French language as fundamental protected characteristics of the State.
  • Prohibits several public bodies from using public funds to challenge certain laws protecting Québec's autonomy.
  • Establishes a 5-member Constitutional Council providing opinions on the interpretation of the Constitution or federal initiatives.
  • Requires an owner to notify the minister before selling a building to a federal institution, in certain cases.
  • Allows the government to adopt directives to counter federal encroachments on Québec's jurisdictions.
  • Specifies that, in the event of a conflict, the right to equality between women and men prevails over freedom of religion.
26627:
• Proclaims the third Friday of October as National Homelessness Awareness Day.
  • This date coincides with the Nuit des sans-abris, held since 1989.
  • The Act aims to highlight homelessness as a collective responsibility affecting individuals and society.
  • No concrete funding or program measures are provided, only symbolic recognition.
  • Comes into force on the date the Act is assented to.
26643: • Divides union dues into two parts: a main due and a separate optional due.,- Requires a majority secret ballot vote of members to set or change the amount of the main due.,- Reserves the optional due for funding political, legal or advocacy activities outside the collective agreement.,- Imposes a voting period of at least 24 hours for votes on dues, strikes or collective agreements.,- Requires associations to present their audited financial statements and a detailed expense report every year.,- Requires disclosure of salaries, benefits and expenses over $5,000 for elected officers.,- Provides for fines of $5,000 to $50,000 for non-compliance with these new obligations.
26675:
• Registration of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles: new annual additional duty (up to $125).
  • Threshold for the additional duty on luxury vehicles raised from $40,000 to $62,500; exemption removed for electric/hybrid vehicles.
  • The Institut de la statistique du Québec will be allowed to collect and share more data with researchers affiliated with public bodies.
  • New formula for calculating the seizable portion of a support debtor's income; support payments for an adult child excluded from seizures.
  • Support debtors receiving social assistance exempted from providing security to collect support payments.
  • Targets for reducing the government's net debt revised upward for 2032-2033 and 2037-2038.
  • Funding for the Fonds Avenir Mécénat Culture increased from $5 million to $6 million.
26685:
• Establishes a system where each patient will be affiliated with a family physician or nurse practitioner, managed by territory.
  • The Régie de l'assurance maladie will determine a vulnerability level for each insured person, based on medical information.
  • General practitioners will be paid by capitation (a fixed amount per patient taken in charge according to their vulnerability), in addition to an hourly rate.
  • A "collective supplement" will be paid to physicians who meet access and service quality targets, set by regulation.
  • Prohibits physicians and their federations from engaging in concerted actions that harm access to care or the training of future professionals.
  • The minister may impose weekly schedules on physicians in certain settings to ensure their presence.
  • Provides for sanctions (reduction of remuneration, disciplinary measures, withholding of contributions) in the event of non-compliance with these rules.
26745:
• Allows the Cercle des ex-parlementaires to create different categories of members according to its by-laws.
  • Opens the door to external members, without voting rights or the possibility of being a director.
  • Modifies the composition of the board of directors, whose directors are elected or appointed according to the by-laws.
  • Authorizes the creation of an executive committee of three to five members of the board.
  • The chair of the board of directors automatically becomes chair of the executive committee.
  • The board of directors determines by by-law the powers delegated to the executive committee.
26771: • Merges the Institut national de santé publique and INESSS into a single Institut québécois de santé et de services sociaux.,- Santé Québec's board of directors also becomes that of Urgences-santé; Héma-Québec takes over coordination of organ donations.,- Abolishes the Commission d'évaluation de l'enseignement collégial and the Commission de la fonction publique.,- Abolishes the Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale; transfers this plan to Retraite Québec.,- Merges two community funds into a single Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales et d'action communautaire.,- Imposes a two-year probationary period on new state administrators, who may be dismissed on 15 days' notice.,- Reduces certain mandatory government reports and removes the requirement to renew contracting authorizations.
26797:
• Continuation of family allowance payments for 12 months following the death of a child.
  • New refundable tax credit for scientific research and experimental development, replacing the current credits.
  • Modernization of tax credits for the development of e-business.
  • Revision of the rates of the tax credit relating to resources, with a cap of $100 million in eligible expenses over 5 years.
  • New "C" share class at Capital régional et coopératif Desjardins, with a cumulative purchase cap of $45,000 per person.
  • Prohibition on retailers decanting bulk tobacco, subject to penalty.
  • Increase in certain public services tax rates and addition of new exemptions.
26821:
• Creates a mixed electoral system: 129 seats in the National Assembly, including 80 constituency seats and 49 regional seats.
  • Divides Québec into 80 constituencies and 17 electoral regions based on administrative regions.
  • Allows each elector to vote twice: one vote for a local candidate, one vote for a regional list or independent candidate.
  • Requires a party to obtain at least 4% of the votes in Québec to receive regional seats.
  • Imposes parity: alternating male-female regional lists, and 40% to 60% female candidates per party in general elections.
  • Provides rules for filling vacant seats based on the regional list or the next-ranked candidate in the election.
  • Adjusts public funding and election spending limits to account for the new types of candidacies.
26823:
• Moves up the coming into force date of the act on the needs of the population in the event of a strike or lock-out.
  • The act in question will come into force upon assent, rather than on November 30, 2025.
  • No other changes to the content of the original act on strikes and lock-outs.
26827:
• The document concerns only the formalities of tabling and publication of the bill, not its content.
  • The actual content of the proposed changes for Le Country Club de Montréal is not provided in this text.
  • It is not possible to summarize the concrete measures of the act based on the information available here.
26829: • Merges Beneva Mutual and The Gore Mutual Insurance Company into a single structure.,- Converts Gore into a share capital company, while creating a temporary management mutual for its members.,- Policyholders with insurance contracts at Gore automatically become members of the new entity.,- Allows for a future merger (before 2027) between The Gore Insurance Company and Unica Insurance Inc.,- Temporarily relaxes (until 2026) the rules on significant shareholdings in decisions concerning Gore.,- Maintains the existing rights and obligations of both companies despite the reorganization.,- Amends the act governing Beneva Mutual to take this new insurer amalgamation into account.
26835:
• The document provided is purely procedural and does not describe the actual content of the bill.
  • It therefore does not make it possible to summarize the concrete changes planned for the Monastère des Ursulines de Québec.
26849: • The Auditor General would be appointed on the joint recommendation of the Premier and the leaders of all parties represented in the National Assembly.,- The appointment would require the approval of two-thirds of the members of the National Assembly.,- A person who has held a senior position on a full-time basis within the past five years could not become Auditor General.,- The senior positions referred to include state administrator, delegate general, delegate, head of post, or head of a government agency.
26893: • Extends the ban on religious symbols to staff of childcare centres (CPEs), subsidized daycares, and subsidized private schools.,- Requires that faces be uncovered to receive childcare, higher education, or certain public services.,- Prohibits religious practice in places under the authority of the organizations covered by the Act, subject to exceptions (health care, private residences, etc.).,- Prohibits an exclusively religious diet in institutional food services.,- Imposes stricter rules on religious accommodations: only minimal constraint permitted, with exclusions related to the sex/gender of the service provider.,- Prohibits the use of a public road or park for collective religious practice without municipal authorization, on pain of a fine.,- Prevents a private institution founded on religious precepts or that selects on the basis of religion from obtaining government accreditation.
26903:
• Ticket resale platforms must clearly warn that the tickets are being resold and that regular tickets may be cheaper.
  • It is prohibited to charge a fee for transferring a show ticket to another person.
  • The resale price of a ticket cannot exceed the official price, unless agreed upon in advance with the show's producer.
  • Producers, sellers, and resellers must promptly notify customers of a cancellation or change of schedule or venue.
  • Merchants must offer an easy-to-find online button to cancel a subscription without giving a reason.
  • Written notice is mandatory, 2 to 10 days before the end of a promotion, indicating the new price that will apply.
  • It is prohibited to prevent a consumer from posting a review or comment about a merchant or its products/services.
26905:
• Requires brain magnetic resonance imaging (or CT scan) during medical examinations of fighters.
  • Adds detailed neurological tests, including the SCAT6/SCOAT6 concussion assessment tool.
  • Requires that all medical examinations be conducted in Québec, regardless of the competitor's place of residence.
  • Sets a maximum period of 30 days between the medical examination and the holding of the fight.
  • Reduces from 2 months to 30 days the time allowed for the medical examination related to a licence application.
  • Requires the organizer to bear the costs of competitors' medical examinations.
  • Allows the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux to adjust the regulation without prior government approval.
26923:
• Prohibits subsidized childcare services from using independent labour or for-profit placement agencies.
  • Allows an exception if the agency is a non-profit organization or a cooperative.
  • Allows the government to create exceptions by regulation depending on the territory or trade concerned.
  • Allows the minister to temporarily authorize a non-compliant agency in exceptional circumstances.
  • Requires authorized agencies to have $2 million in liability insurance and to report certain refusals.
  • Prohibits agencies from soliciting providers' staff or imposing non-competition clauses on them.
  • Provides for fines of $1,000 to $75,000 depending on the type of offender in the event of an offence.
26925:
• The Minister of Economy must now reduce the regulatory burden on businesses; the government may amend regulations to that effect.
  • Departments will have to remove 1 or 2 administrative formalities for each new requirement proposed.
  • Removal of the Québec residency requirement in certain sectors (real estate brokerage, funeral services, transportation).
  • Creation of a new mandatory permit ("certification") to drive an escort vehicle accompanying an oversized vehicle on the road.
  • Extension of the validity of certain permits, such as the one for operating a maple grove for maple syrup production purposes.
  • Easing of rules for the manufacturing, bottling and transportation of alcoholic beverages by third parties.
  • Possible creation of forestry pilot projects and elimination of several activity reporting requirements within the State.
26927:
• The seller of a used vehicle must guarantee that it is free of any undeclared right.
  • The seller must provide a SAAQ verification notice before the sale.
  • A fine of $200 to $300 applies if the seller fails to meet this obligation.
  • The SAAQ will be required to check the register of personal and movable real rights for sales between private individuals.
  • A compensation scheme is created for a buyer harmed by an omission in the verification notice.
  • Used car dealers will be required to record the result of this verification on the vehicle's label.
  • The seller must pay off any mortgages encumbering the vehicle, unless otherwise agreed with the buyer.
26931:
• The document provided is essentially administrative and does not detail the actual content of the powers granted to the Ville de Rivière-du-Loup.
  • It only confirms the steps of tabling and publication of the bill, without specifying the concrete measures.
  • A reliable summary of the powers granted is not possible based on this truncated text.
26939: • Creates a new offence for any undue influence on voting during a party leadership campaign or nomination contest.,- Prohibits offering gifts, loans, jobs or benefits to obtain or change a vote in these campaigns.,- Also prohibits threats aimed at influencing a person's vote in these internal processes.,- Provides for fines of $5,000 to $20,000 for a first offence under the Election Act.,- Provides for fines of $10,000 to $30,000 for a repeat offence within 10 years.,- Exempts food or beverages offered at private gatherings or by official representatives.,- Specifies that a campaign to designate a party leader or spokesperson is considered a leadership campaign.
26941: • The government may designate, for a period of 5 years, "priority projects of national scope" deemed strategic.,- A single government authorization replaces multiple permits normally required from various ministries and municipalities.,- The Minister of Finance may authorize preparatory work even before the official authorization is granted.,- Relief measures apply to environmental, mining, forestry, agricultural and municipal rules for these projects.,- A public consultation through the BAPE replaces other consultation mechanisms provided for under the usual laws.,- The government may amend, suspend, revoke or allow the transfer of an authorization already granted.,- The inspection, investigation and administrative sanction powers of the relevant authorities remain applicable despite the single authorization.
26949:
• Creates a committee that decides whether information on sex offenders at high risk of reoffending is publicly disclosed, for a maximum of 3 years.
  • Prohibits protesting within 50 metres of the residence of a member of the National Assembly, an elected municipal official, or an elected prefect.
  • Prohibits possessing or throwing dangerous objects during a protest; allows police to search without a warrant when there are reasonable grounds.
  • Prohibits publicly displaying symbols of entities listed on a list of "entities with criminal purposes" established by the minister.
  • Allows for the creation of Indigenous police boards to manage a common police force across several communities.
  • Allows for increased sharing of police services (patrol, investigations, emergency response) between police forces.
  • Allows victims to read their own written statements themselves at parole hearings.
26959:
• Amends the Act respecting the governance of the health and social services system.
  • Prohibits excluding a community organization from a financial assistance program because of a social economy project.
  • Applies to grants intended for community organizations in health and social services.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
26971:
• Creates a new status of "person in charge of an educational childcare service in the community" outside of a private residence.
  • Coordinating offices for home childcare become responsible for the "in the community" component as well.
  • Sets a maximum of 6 children alone, 9 with an assistant, or 12 for two persons in charge working in collaboration.
  • Allows two recognized persons to share the same premises through a mandatory collaboration agreement.
  • Prohibits tolerating abusive or degrading behaviour toward children among collaborating persons.
  • Gives the coordinating office the power to order the evacuation of a location in the event of serious danger to children.
  • Extends the existing collective representation and bargaining regime to these new persons in charge.
26993: • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without government approval, in accordance with guidelines from the Office.,- The Office des professions, rather than the government, will now approve codes of ethics and diplomas leading to a permit.,- Nurses will be able to initiate and prescribe more examinations, tests and medications in accordance with forthcoming regulations.,- Midwives will be able to prescribe contraceptives and treat certain sexually transmitted infections in any person.,- Certain restrictions on medications and care that optometrists may prescribe will be removed.,- Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a separate specific permit.,- New rules govern financial benefits between pharmacists, manufacturers and pharmacy chains.
26995:
• Postpones from January 1 to February 28, 2026 the coming into force of several provisions on access to medical services.
  • Also postpones certain 2025 deadlines to February 27, 2026, in keeping with this additional delay.
  • Amends future application dates (2027, 2028) to align them with a fiscal year beginning April 1.
  • Adjusts the deadlines of national objective No. 5 concerning dates in 2026 and 2027.
  • Completely repeals Chapter VIII of the Act, namely sections 130 to 207.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
27049: • Removes the government's power to impose, by regulation, the methods of remuneration for health professionals.,- Allows remuneration agreements including capitation payment, individual or collective, for physicians.,- Encourages the care of all insured persons and the monitoring of service quality.,- Designates up to 180,000 vulnerable persons who are automatically considered registered once taken in charge by a family physician.,- This measure regarding vulnerable persons applies retroactively from the introduction of the bill.,- Increases the budgets provided for medical remuneration, rising to more than $5.2 billion depending on the categories.,- Abolishes the representative body for general practitioners, keeping only the one for specialist physicians.
27053:
• Renames the Act and broadens its scope: it now governs the exploration and exploitation of underground reservoirs and fluids such as hydrogen, not just gas.
  • Requires a mandatory licence to explore or exploit an underground reservoir or certain fluids below the arable layer.
  • Allows the Minister to suspend the granting of licences or reserve territories for the State, particularly in urban or protected areas.
  • Requires licence holders to enter into an agreement with holders of mining rights on the same territory, failing which an external decision-maker rules on the matter.
  • Makes documents submitted to the Minister by licence holders public, subject to exceptions provided for by regulation.
  • Authorizes the government to establish pilot exploration or exploitation projects for a maximum period of 5 to 7 years.
  • Allows municipalities, under certain conditions, to prevent certain work related to these activities within their territory.
27079: • Creates a single window for applying for affordable or low-cost rental housing.,- Allows the rent of an affordable housing unit to be set even in a new or converted building.,- Requires tenants to provide their income information; compensation may be required if not eligible.,- Prohibits the subletting of affordable rental housing.,- Specifies the rules for student tenants, including proof of full-time enrollment.,- Allows part of a co-ownership's contingency fund to be invested long-term.,- Authorizes the sale of surplus public buildings for housing purposes, sometimes free of charge.
27099:
• Abolishes the requirement for physicians to perform particular medical activities in order to adhere to an agreement.
  • Removes the requirement to develop territorial and institutional medical and dental workforce plans.
  • Repeals the law requiring a physician to obtain authorization from Santé Québec to become non-participating.
  • Creates a "mixed-practice professional" status, subject to an agreement for only part of their practice.
  • Allows the creation of mixed specialized medical centres, combining participating and non-participating physicians.
  • Removes bed limits and the 24-hour hospitalization limit in specialized medical centres.
  • Ends, no later than three months after the coming into force, existing agreements related to particular medical activities.
27127:
• Creates a national air quality strategy to inform and protect the public.
  • Aims to modernize air quality standards in accordance with World Health Organization recommendations.
  • Provides for a real-time index informing citizens of contaminant levels in the air.
  • Calls for increasing air quality measurement instruments and expanding urban greening.
  • Aims to regulate construction near risk zones, such as major roads.
  • Requires the government to adopt a five-year action plan with specific targets and public monitoring.
  • The first action plan must be published within 18 months of the act's passage.
27173:
• Sets a target of reducing food waste by 50% by 2030.
  • Requires the minister to develop a multi-year action plan to achieve this objective.
  • Requires processors, distributors and retailers to offer agreements to recognized organizations for their unsold goods.
  • Prioritizes local and regional organizations in these agreement offers.
  • Provides for possible exemptions, notably for small retailers.
  • Allows the minister to impose an agreement with Recyc-Québec if no agreement is reached.
  • Imposes fines of $250 to $6,000 for non-compliance with obligations.
27177: • Creates a regional immigration table in each administrative region of Québec.,- These tables bring together the minister, prefects, mayors and Indigenous representatives of the region.,- Each table must develop a regional immigration plan to be revised every five years.,- The plan covers reception capacity, labour needs and regional immigration targets.,- The minister must consult the tables and take the plans into account in their decisions.,- Gives municipalities the power to act in immigration, reception and integration.,- A new immigration rule would not automatically apply to persons already present in Québec.
27247:
• Modernizes judicial ethics: clarifies the complaint process, review and investigation of a judge
  • Adds new possible sanctions against judges at fault, including suspension without pay for up to 6 months
  • Makes public the decisions of the Conseil de la magistrature on ethics complaints
  • Clarifies the roles of the chief judge: ensuring justice is rendered promptly and diligently
  • Changes the composition of the Conseil de la magistrature and assigns the vice-presidency to the chief municipal judge
  • Allows substitute judges to be paid by the half-day and compensates deliberation time
  • Changes the maximum age for participation in judges' pension plans, raising it to 71 years
27261: • Replaces the "serious and immediate danger" criterion with a broader "situation where a danger exists" criterion to justify forced confinement.,- Reduces the maximum temporary confinement period from 72 to 48 hours before a psychiatric examination must confirm its necessity.,- Allows adults living with a mental disorder to draft advance psychiatric directives to consent to future care in the event of temporary incapacity.,- Creates "coordinated action processes" among stakeholders (police, health services, public curator, etc.) to coordinate interventions with at-risk individuals.,- Requires the minister to conclude a national framework agreement and regional coordination mechanisms to govern these interventions.,- Makes legal aid free, regardless of income, for cases related to institutional confinement or care authorization.,- Requires a certificate of no impediment for staff regularly in contact with vulnerable children in certain institutions.
27263:
• The provided text contains only procedural documents (report and publication notice), not the content of the bill.
  • It is therefore impossible to reliably summarize the concrete measures concerning the Ville de Gatineau.
27275:
• Authorizes the government to draw $32.12 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for 2026-2027.
  • This amount covers approximately 28.2% of the total appropriations to be voted for the year, allocated by department.
  • The Treasury Board may transfer appropriations between programs, up to 15% of the authorized amount.
  • Approves projected expenditures of $6.6 billion for the government's special funds.
  • Approves projected investments of $1.6 billion for these same special funds.
  • Details the amounts allocated by portfolio: health ($10.1 billion), education ($4.7 billion), transport ($737 million), among others.
  • The Act comes into force upon official assent.
27291: • Allows municipalities to acquire buildings with unpaid taxes for 3 years or more, under certain conditions,- Authorizes the sale of small low-value lots to neighbouring owners,- Broadens municipalities' right to purchase or build buildings to lease to non-profit organizations or daycares,- Adds possible energy efficiency standards to municipal building by-laws,- Abolishes the property tax exemption for certain rectories, starting in 2027,- Removes the maximum ceiling on amounts a municipality can set aside in a financial reserve,- Specifies that non-profit organizations are not commercial establishments under the act on municipal grants
27295: • Prohibits using a person's identity or image without their consent to advertise to a consumer.,- The definition of image also includes modified versions or recordings that appear to represent the person, such as deepfakes.,- Gives the president of the Office de la protection du consommateur the power to order the cessation of prohibited business practices.,- Allows the president to order anyone to preserve evidence during an inspection or investigation.,- The Autorité des marchés financiers exercises these same powers for representations related to the financial sector.,- Failure to comply with an order from the president may result in penal or administrative sanctions.,- Businesses could be excluded from public contracts if they receive such an order.
27297: • Extends from two to five years the period during which an elector absent from Québec may vote by mail.,- Allows students abroad to vote by mail for the entire duration of their studies.,- Requires proof of school enrollment for electors absent for study purposes.,- Amends the deadlines applicable to registration applications for voting outside Québec, extending them to five years.
27343:
• The Minister of Labour, rather than the government, will henceforth decree amendments to collective agreement decrees.
  • The Minister will be able to approve, amend or repeal the by-laws of joint committees, and issue directives on their governance.
  • Regulates the non-renewal of a decree: notice required six months before its expiry, decree ceasing one year afterward.
  • Allows the government to establish sectoral labour standards when a decree expires, replacing it.
  • Removes the obligation to publish notices in newspapers and to annually submit certain financial documents to the Minister.
  • Clarifies the rules for health and safety representatives on construction sites, particularly at the start and completion of work.
  • Allows the Commission de la construction du Québec to create a supplementary preventive withdrawal plan for pregnant or breastfeeding workers.
27345:
• Creates a new Self-Directed Personal Assistance Program with financial assistance, administered by Retraite Québec.
  • Persons with disabilities choose their own service providers and the terms of assistance.
  • Eligibility is conditional on residing in Québec, except for those living in a substitute living environment.
  • The benefit includes a base amount based on required hours, which may be increased for special needs.
  • Providers may perform actions that the person with disabilities would do themselves if not for their disability.
  • Provides for recourse through review before Retraite Québec, then before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • Retraite Québec must produce annual reports and an assessment after five years, tabled with the National Assembly.
27347: • The bill amends the Flag and Emblems of Québec Act.,- It officially recognizes the “Plaid du Québec” as the tartan of Québec.,- This tartan is already registered in the Scottish Register of Tartans.,- Its colours (blue, green, red, gold, white) reflect those of Québec's coat of arms.,- The white recalls the scroll bearing the motto “Je me souviens.”,- The Act would come into force on the date of its assent.
27349: • Joint exercise of parental authority by both parents can no longer be automatically presumed to be in the child's best interest.,- Custody granted to a parent found to be violent is presumed contrary to the child's best interest, unless proven otherwise.,- That parent will have to prove sufficient guarantees for the safety of the other parent and the child.,- Unproven allegations of family violence cannot be used against the parent who reports it or who is a victim.,- Actions taken to protect oneself or the child are presumed not to be relevant in custody decisions.,- These changes also apply to disputes over the exercise of parental authority, not only custody.
27351:
• The text provided concerns only the filing and publication formalities of the bill, not its content.
  • It is impossible to summarize the concrete changes related to the building in question, due to lack of available information.
  • The document only confirms that the required legal notices were published in accordance with the rules.
27461:
• Renews the notwithstanding clause of the Charter of the French Language, section 214.
  • Also renews the notwithstanding clause provided for in section 217 of the Act respecting French, the common language of Québec.
  • These clauses override the application of certain sections of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
  • The sections concerned are those guaranteeing certain fundamental freedoms and legal rights (sections 2 and 7 to 15).
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
27463:
• Requires the Commission de la représentation électorale to publish a new list of electoral divisions
  • Maintains the current limits of 4 electoral divisions in Gaspésie–Bas-Saint-Laurent and 8 on the Island of Montréal
  • Sets the coming into force of this new list according to the end date of the 43rd legislature
  • Sets the number of electoral divisions in Québec at 127
  • Removes the former limit of 122 to 125 electoral divisions provided for by the Act
  • Creates a 3-member committee to review the criteria for delimiting electoral divisions
  • The committee must consult various stakeholders and submit a report before February 1, 2028
27465: • Creates a Committee on Complementary and Integrative Health Approaches within INESSS.,- This committee assesses the effectiveness, safety and risks of these approaches (e.g., acupuncture, chiropractic).,- The committee may recommend that certain services related to these approaches be reimbursed by the RAMQ.,- Expands the mandate of the Fonds de recherche du Québec to include these approaches and the determinants of health.,- Requires the Minister of Higher Education to fund university programs related to these approaches.,- The committee has 8 members appointed by the minister, including experts in integrative health.,- Provides for ethics rules and conflict-of-interest management for committee members.
27467: • Limits the use of the Charter's notwithstanding clause to a serious and objective threat or the protection of French and Indigenous languages,- Prohibits any override of the right to life and other fundamental rights protected under section 1,- Requires a report from the Minister of Justice analyzing the impacts before any bill invoking the notwithstanding clause,- Imposes a requirement for an advisory opinion from the Court of Appeal on the legality of the proposed override,- Requires a general consultation in a parliamentary committee before the adoption of such a law,- Requires the support of two-thirds of members, from at least two parties, to adopt an override,- Limits the maximum duration of a provision overriding the Charter to five years
27655:
• Recognizes the right to food: physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food.
  • Requires the government to take measures to give effect to and protect this right to food.
  • Creates the National Committee on the Right to Food, made up of representatives from various sectors (community, Indigenous, school, health, agri-food, municipal).
  • The Committee advises the government, monitors the development of the right, and publishes a report at least every 3 years.
  • The government must assess the impact of its decisions on the right to food and mitigate any negative effects.
  • Aims in particular at access to adequate food at school and the reduction of food waste.
  • Amends the Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms to include this new right to food.
27657:
• Recognizes the right of older persons to remain at home for as long as possible.
  • Guarantees access to affordable and adapted housing, and to financial security.
  • Protects against physical, psychological or financial abuse.
  • Entrusts the Commission des droits de la personne with monitoring compliance with these rights.
  • Creates a national strategy for the autonomy and home support of older persons.
  • Requires the government to publish a five-year action plan with concrete targets.
  • Provides for tax measures, rent regulation and support for caregivers.
27659:
• Reduces the base contribution rate for the Québec Pension Plan.
  • Increases the small business deduction rate for certain corporations.
  • Introduces a temporary exemption from contributions to the Health Services Fund for agricultural, forestry and fishing employers.
  • Extends and expands the tax credit for employment in the Gaspé Peninsula, including seafood processing.
  • Extends the tax credit for print media to news agencies and media broadcasting news bulletins.
  • Extends the tax credit for the digital transformation of print media, but gradually reduces its rate.
  • Eases the eligibility criteria for certain cultural tax credits and adjusts those related to artificial intelligence.
27679: • Allows a worried person ("person at risk") to request information about their intimate partner considered dangerous.,- A minor 14 years of age or older may make this information request on their own.,- The Sûreté du Québec conducts the search and then transmits the relevant information to a designated body.,- A designated person meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information and direct them to resources.,- The intimate partner concerned has no right to know that a request exists or to access the information collected.,- Provides for fines of $500 to $30,000 for false statements or prohibited disclosure of information.,- Revises the rules on the disclosure to victims of information concerning persons who are incarcerated or on conditional release.
27681:
• Proclaims November 5 as National Awareness Day for the issues faced by immunosuppressed persons.
  • Aims to inform the public about the increased risk of infections among immunosuppressed persons.
  • Recalls the symbol of the tilted red "i" adopted in 2023 to encourage social distancing.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
27683:
• Prohibits booking platforms from preventing hoteliers from freely setting their prices.
  • Also prevents platforms from limiting discounts or benefits offered by operators.
  • Any contractual clause contrary to this freedom is automatically considered invalid.
  • Applies to contracts between digital platforms and tourist accommodation operators.
  • The Act comes into force upon its official assent.
27695:
• Creates a mandatory "co-construction" process with First Nations and Inuit for laws and regulations that concern them.
  • Requires a preliminary analysis to determine whether a measure affects them, before initiating co-construction.
  • Requires contact with Indigenous organizations at least six months before a bill or regulation is introduced.
  • Creates a legislative reconciliation secretariat within the Ministère du Conseil exécutif to coordinate this process.
  • Provides for mediation or another mechanism if no consensus is reached between the parties.
  • Requires the government to review existing laws to make them consistent with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
  • Requires a government report on the implementation of the Act, tabled in the National Assembly every five years.
27705:
• Permanently fixes the electoral divisions of Gaspé and Bonaventure, despite the usual delimitation rules.
  • Increases the total number of electoral divisions in Québec to 126.
  • Also maintains the current boundaries of Matane-Matapédia-Mitis and Rimouski.
  • Requires the Commission de la représentation to publish a new list of electoral divisions.
  • Provides that this new list will come into force according to the end date of the 43rd legislature.
  • Creates a three-member committee to review the criteria for delimiting electoral divisions.
  • This committee must consult citizens and experts, and submit a report before February 1, 2028.
27715:
• Vocational training and adult general education must be offered in French.
  • This requirement applies to school service centres and subsidized private schools.
  • English remains permitted for persons already eligible for English instruction under the Charter of the French Language.
  • It becomes prohibited to allow a person to receive these services in English without being eligible to do so.
  • Penalties are provided for institutions that do not comply with this prohibition.
  • Persons already enrolled in English before June 30, 2028, will be able to complete their program in that language.
  • The Act will come into force on July 1, 2028.
27731:
• Authorizes the government to pay out $81,686,460,965 in appropriations for the 2026-2027 fiscal year.
  • Health and Social Services receives the largest share, more than $30 billion.
  • Education receives approximately $12.6 billion, and Higher Education $6.6 billion.
  • Allows the Treasury Board to authorize transfers of appropriations between programs, up to 15% of the amount.
  • Approves the expenditure and investment forecasts of numerous special funds for 2026-2027.
  • Approves an overexpenditure of special funds of more than $2 billion for 2024-2025.
  • Provides for net appropriations that may increase if associated revenues exceed forecasts.
27741:
• Prohibits social media from registering users under 16, with mandatory age verification.
  • Requires platforms to inform users of screen-related risks and attention-capturing mechanisms.
  • Requires tools to track and limit time spent on social media.
  • Prohibits certain mechanisms that encourage engagement in video games for those under 13.
  • Prohibits paid random loot boxes and microtransactions in video games for those under 18.
  • Requires video game manufacturers to inform users of risks and incentive mechanisms used.
  • Merchants have 12 months to verify the age of already registered users and terminate non-compliant accounts.
27745:
• Prohibits selling an energy drink to a person under 16 years of age.
  • Prohibits persons under 16 from buying such drinks or posing as older to buy them.
  • Sellers must require photo identification if there is doubt about the person's age.
  • Prohibits online sales or sales through vending machines, except for exceptions provided by regulation.
  • Fines of $100 for minors, $500 to $1,500 for adults in violation.
  • Merchants face fines of $2,500 to $62,500 depending on the case.
  • Santé Québec gains inspection and investigation powers to verify compliance with the Act.
27753:
• Creates a new position of "special clerk" to support the courts in their adjudicative functions.
  • Requires a minimum of 5 years' experience as a lawyer or notary to be appointed to this position.
  • Establishes a 5-year, renewable term, with a selection and renewal process governed by regulation.
  • Provides for a complaint and ethics process, including investigations and possible sanctions (reprimand, suspension, removal from office).
  • Designates a "coordinating special clerk" responsible for overseeing and distributing the work of special clerks.
  • Sets the remuneration, employee benefits, and pension plan of special clerks by government regulation.
  • Amends several existing acts to replace references to "clerk" with "special clerk" or "judge," as the case may be.
27827: • Allows a property owner to sign a voluntary contract to protect the biodiversity of their land.,- The contract may be entered into with a municipality, an environmental non-profit organization, or an Indigenous nation or community.,- The contract must be notarized and registered in the land register to be valid.,- The obligations may last for up to 99 years.,- The contract must precisely describe the monitoring and evaluation measures planned.,- The contract must specify the conditions under which it may be amended or terminated.
